newsitem.title: USA: M.A.Hanna backs low end of estimate range.
newsitem.headline: M.A.Hanna backs low end of estimate range.

text.p: M.A. Hanna Co president Douglas McGregor, who will become chief executive officer in January, said Hanna is comfortable with the low end of 1996 earnings estimates of $1.25-$1.30 a share.
Hanna earned $1.07 a share in 1995, taking into consideration a June 1996 three-for-two stock split.
"If you look at the First Call estimates of $1.25-$1.30, I think we're comfortable at the lower end of that range right now," McGregor said in a telephone interview.
"That would give us an earnings improvement year over year of about 17 percent, which ain't too shabby," he added.

Asked about the 1997 range of $1.40-$1.50, he said the company does not predict future-year earnings. "We're just putting our plans together for the year," he said. "But the range has usually been pretty accurate."
